newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude slips in rangebound trade late session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude slips in rangebound trade late session.

text.p: NYMEX crude prices slipped Tuesday afternoon but were rangebound as expectations of this evening's weekly oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) failed to provide market direction.
"The estimates are the same as last week's, so it's like 'who cares'" said a crude dealer of the API data expectations.
"There is nothing going on. We have been trading between $23.80 and $23.25 and it's going to remain that way (until the close)," the trader said.
At 1448 EST, March crude was off one cent at $23.93 a barrel.
Expiry-related rolling continued to pressure February heating oil which was off 0.44 cent at 66.85 cents a gallon.
Feb gasoline was off 0.42 cent a gallon at 67.20 cents, also giving way to some front-to-back month selling ahead of the Feb refined product contract expiry Friday.
"There is some selling of Feb for March, but it's pretty dead here," said a gasoline trader, noting thin volume.

A consensus of trader estimates for the API data called for a draw in distillate stocks of two million barrels, while gasoline and crude stocks were expected to build by 2.25 million and three million barrels respectively.
The data reflects the week ended January 24.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
